title: An Effective String Theory Toolbox for Quantum Hall Interfaces I: Worldsheet Kinematics and Constraint Structure
abstract: A freely moving quantum Hall interface is fundamentally different from an ordinary edge fixed by an external confining potential. Since a normal displacement changes the areas occupied by the adjacent incompressible phases, the interface geometry and charge dynamics cannot be treated as independent degrees of freedom. We formulate this problem for interfaces between Abelian quantum Hall phases using a spatially reparametrization-invariant worldsheet description, in which tangential motion is a relabeling of the interface while normal motion is physical. Starting from the two-sided Chern--Simons response, we derive the relation between normal charge transport and interface motion. We then introduce a relative-area construction, defined with respect to a material reference curve, that converts this velocity relation into an equal-time constraint linking the charged boundary sector to the interface shape. Combined with the folded $K$-matrix current algebra, this identifies the universal Hall kinematics of the moving interface while leaving its geometric energy and neutral dynamics dependent on microscopic interface physics. The resulting framework provides a systematic basis for effective theories of dynamical quantum Hall interfaces.
summary: This work develops an effective field theory toolbox for understanding dynamically moving quantum Hall interfaces. It rigorously links the interface's geometric motion to its electrical charge transport using a worldsheet formalism derived from Chern-Simons theory. The resulting framework cleanly separates universal topological kinematics from material-dependent physics.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of formulating an effective, geometrically consistent theory for quantum Hall (QH) interfaces where interface motion is coupled to charge dynamics.
main_result: A systematic framework is derived that separates the universal Hall kinematics of the moving interface from its microscopic geometric and neutral energy contributions.
method: The authors employ a worldsheet description, starting from the two-sided Chern-Simons response and introducing a relative-area construction to derive an equal-time constraint linking charge transport to interface shape.
model_or_system: The system models Abelian quantum Hall interfaces separating incompressible phases. The analysis uses concepts from topological field theory (Chern-Simons action) applied to the geometry of the moving boundary.
key_observables: Normal charge current ($\mathbf{J} \cdot \mathbf{n}$), interface velocity ($v_n$), relative magnetic-area density ($a_\sigma$), and geometric energy terms.

paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the kinematic constraints from the Chern-Simons response, deriving an equal-time constraint via relative area construction, and finally separating the resulting dynamics into universal Hall kinematics and microscopic geometric terms.
why_interesting: While focused on QH physics, the development of a general worldsheet formalism for constrained boundary dynamics is highly relevant to modeling interfaces in other strongly correlated systems or topological materials where geometry dictates charge transport.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Frenet frame and level-set description of a quantum Hall interface. The solid curve is the level set F = 0, the QH fluid occupies F < 0, and n points from the QH phase toward the other phase.

FIG. 2. Relative-area construction and local swept-area kinematics. Left: a fixed material reference loop X0(σ) is connected to the physical interface X(τ, σ) by a smooth interpolation Y (τ, σ, r), defining the relative magnetic-area density aσ. Right: normal motion sweeps magnetic area at the local rate B√γ vn, leading in the material sector to Qmat ≡φ′ c −∆ν aσ = 0. The local density depends on the chosen material pairing and interpolation, whereas its integral gives the signed relative magnetic area B[A[X] −A[X0]].

FIG. 3. Two-stage local canonical reduction. The first-class constraint Hσ generates spatial relabeling and is removed by quotienting by Diff+(S1). About a straight equilibrium interface with ∆ν ̸= 0, the nonzero modes of (χA, C⊥, πλ) form a second-class system and are eliminated through the Dirac bracket. After fixing the nonpropagating conserved profiles retained by the auxiliary completion, the resulting local worldsheet sector contains the charged shape sector together with any neutral modes not gapped by allowed interface interactions.
